title: Anode and Graphite Q3 2026 Price Review
author: Benchmark Team
text: The divergence between natural and synthetic anode active material (AAM) prices observed earlier in the year stopped widening in Q3, with prices across both chemistries and all capacities remaining flat from mid-June- to mid-September.However, this midstream stability contrasted with continued movement in the feedstock markets during the same period, notably for coke materials, with pre-calcined pet coke prices rising 6.5% across July and August.“Q3 was characterised by a clear standoff between rising synthetic graphite feedstock costs and an oversupplied AAM market,” said Tony Alderson, anode and graphite research manager at Benchmark. “Producers absorbed the additional cost pressure rather than risk raising prices and losing market share. Meanwhile, coarser natural graphite flake grades continued to soften globally, whilst finer mesh material remained stable after reaching already depressed price lows from Q4 2025.”Why did anode prices stay flat despite rising feedstock costs?AAM oversupply is set to be nearly 250ktpa in 2026 and has kept downstream buyer leverage strong enough to prevent producers passing through the renewed rise in coke costs seen this quarter. In Q2, when synthetic producers were able to pass on price increases, but with EV and ESS demand growth failing to notably outpace capacity additions, both natural and synthetic producers have absorbed the cost pressure into margins in Q3.Cell manufacturers were also reluctant to increase bid prices, partly because of the introduction of China’s 2% lithium battery consumption tax at the start of September. As a result, existing orders continued to be fulfilled at current contract prices, while new pricing agreements remained under negotiation into October.What's driving synthetic graphite feedstock costs higher?Coke costs resumed their climb through Q3 on the back of renewed geopolitical risk. Renewed tensions around the Strait of Hormuz reignited concerns over Middle Eastern crude supply from late June, pushing Brent crude and Chinese slurry prices higher and feeding through the pet coke chain. Low-sulphur pre-calcined pet coke DDP China rose 6.5% between June and August, from RMB 4,200/tonne (USD $617.40) to RMB 4,475/tonne (USD $666.78), whilst pre-calcined pet needle coke, the higher-value feedstock used in EV-grade synthetic AAM, added a further 3.5% over the same timeframe, extending gains already seen earlier in the year.Higher energy costs and growing pressure on graphitisation tolling services also pushed tolling fees up by 2.3% between June and August. This added further cost pressure for synthetic graphite anode producers alongside the increase in feedstock prices.Why is natural graphite flake still under pressure?Natural graphite flake prices diverged by region and mesh size. -100 mesh, 94–95% C DDP China grade remained flat at RMB 3,050/t, extending its multi-month plateau at close to an all-time low.Coarser material weakened modestly in China amidst continued oversupply and lower-than-expected demand from industrial end-use sectors. The +100 mesh, 94–95% C grade fell by 1.9% between June and August, whilst the +80 mesh, 94–95% C grade declined by 0.9%. On an FOB East Asia basis, +80 mesh, 94–95% C material fell by a more moderate 4.2% over the same period.What is expected in Q4 for graphite and anode?In Q4, Benchmark will be watching to see whether the cost/price standoff breaks. If needle and pet coke keep climbing, watch for a delayed pass-through into synthetic AAM prices, echoing Q2's pattern.Further escalation in the Iran war and disruption to the Strait of Hormuz would extend the feedstock cost pressure seen this quarter. Elsewhere, China’s temporary suspension of its expanded export controls to the US is also set to expire in November 2026.Benchmark will also be watching to see if the competitiveness of East African flake graphite producers continues.
